files.purpose: Defines FloatingSidebarPanel, the SwiftUI view that shows the sidebar's thread list as a draggable, resizable floating glass panel over the chat area while the sidebar column is collapsed, replacing the toolbar-button popover. Owns the drag/resize gesture math, clamping to the chat area, and the persisted position and size in app settings.
key_symbols: private func onDrag(rest: CGPoint, size: CGSize) -> (CGSize) -> Void
private static func clamp(_ origin: CGPoint, size: CGSize, in area: CGSize) -> CGPoint
calls_into: glassEffect(.regular, in: shape) SwiftUI Liquid Glass modifier
state_owned: @State private var dragOrigin: CGPoint? - the panel top-left while the strip is held, nil at rest
@State private var grab: CGPoint? - the origin captured on the first tick of a move drag
@State private var resizeStart: CGSize? - the size captured on the first tick of a resize drag
Reads and writes model.settings.sidebarPanelSize and model.settings.sidebarPanelOrigin, which are owned by AppModel rather than this view
side_effects: Writes model.settings.sidebarPanelSize on every resize drag tick, live rather than only on drag end
Writes model.settings.sidebarPanelOrigin once on drag end, from the final clamped dragOrigin
Invokes the injected close() closure when the xmark button is pressed
platform_assumptions: import AppKit for NSCursor.frameResize(position: .bottomRight, directions: .all) used as the resize grip cursor and dragCursor
SwiftUI glassEffect(.regular, in:) requires the macOS Liquid Glass material API
@Environment(AppModel.self) uses the Swift Observation based SwiftUI environment
Top-left origin geometry: offset(x:y:) inside a maxWidth/maxHeight infinite frame aligned .topLeading
Chrome.contentTopInset as the default Y implies a macOS window chrome inset under the title bar
persisted_fields: settings.sidebarPanelSize: CGSize? - optional, nil default, falls back to CGSize(width: 300, height: 560)
settings.sidebarPanelOrigin: CGPoint? - optional, nil default, falls back to CGPoint(x: 12, y: Chrome.contentTopInset)
ui_elements: Top strip of height 44 acting as the drag handle across the panel's full width
Title Text("Threads") at .font(.system(size: 12.5, weight: .medium)), .foregroundStyle(Chrome.primaryText.opacity(0.92))

Title capsule chain: .padding(.horizontal, Chrome.capsuleHorizontalPadding), .frame(height: Chrome.capsuleContentHeight), .padding(.vertical, Chrome.capsuleVerticalPadding), .fixedSize(), .chromeGlassCapsule(), .padding(.top, Chrome.chromeTopPadding), .padding(.leading, Chrome.chromeHorizontalPadding)
The title carries its own PanelDragHandle overlay, with the source comment 'The title is a label, not a control, so it drags the panel too.'
Middle PanelDragHandle with .frame(maxWidth: .infinity), .frame(height: 44), .help("Drag to move"), .accessibilityLabel(Text("Drag to move"))
Close button shown only when canClose: ChromeCircleButton(symbol: "xmark", help: "Back into the column"), .padding(.top, Chrome.chromeTopPadding), .padding(.trailing, Chrome.chromeHorizontalPadding)
Strip layout: HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 8) holding title, drag strip and close button, as an .overlay(alignment: .top)
Bottom-trailing resize grip: PanelDragHandle in .frame(width: 16, height: 16) with .help("Drag to resize"), as an .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing)
Content: SidebarView(inPopover: true, dismiss: nil) with .padding(.top, 44) so the list clears the strip, then .frame(width: size.width, height: size.height)

Inner background: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: HydraPanel.cornerRadius, style: .continuous) filled .clear, .glassEffect(.regular, in: shape), overlaid with shape.fill(Chrome.glassTint.opacity(isDark ? 0.22 : 0.16))
Outer background behind the clip: same shape filled (isDark ? Color.black : Color.white).opacity(isDark ? 0.3 : 0.34) with .shadow(color: .black.opacity(isDark ? 1 : 0.65), radius: 28, y: 10)
Panel body clipped with .clipShape(shape) between the two background layers
Placement: .offset(x: origin.x, y: origin.y) inside .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
feature_notes: Default panel size 300x560 points, minimum 240x320, and a 12 point margin kept from every edge of the chat area

Stored size is clamped per axis as min(max(minSize, stored), max(minSize, area - margin * 2)), so an oversized stored size shrinks to fit but never below the minimum even when the area is smaller than the minimum
Default resting origin is x = 12, y = Chrome.contentTopInset, passed through clamp(_:size:in:)
clamp computes x = min(max(12, x), max(12, area.width - size.width - 12)) and y = min(max(12, y), max(12, area.height - size.height - 12)), so the panel can never be dragged off an edge
Resize is anchored at the current origin: width capped at area.width - origin.x - 12 and height at area.height - origin.y - 12, with the minimum size as the lower bound
Resize persists live on every tick; a move persists only in onDragEnd, with dragOrigin acting as the live preview
grab and resizeStart capture the base value on the gesture's first tick so the translation applies to a fixed base instead of accumulating
Animation .animation(dragOrigin == nil ? Chrome.panelSlide : nil, value: origin): the panel springs to a new resting position but tracks the pointer with no animation while dragged
The close button labelled 'Back into the column' appears only while the sidebar column still exists (canClose) and returns the list to the column
Dark and light differ in glass tint (0.22 vs 0.16), backing fill (black 0.3 vs white 0.34) and shadow alpha (1.0 vs 0.65)
unresolved_questions: Numeric values of Chrome.contentTopInset, Chrome.capsuleHorizontalPadding, Chrome.capsuleContentHeight, Chrome.capsuleVerticalPadding, Chrome.chromeTopPadding, Chrome.chromeHorizontalPadding, Chrome.glassTint, Chrome.primaryText, Chrome.panelSlide and HydraPanel.cornerRadius live outside this bundle
Who constructs FloatingSidebarPanel and what it passes for area, canClose and close is not visible from this file
Whether PanelDragHandle's onDrag receives a cumulative translation is inferred from the grab/resizeStart pattern; its definition is in another file

files.purpose: Implements the sidebar thread row's flight animation when a thread settles or reopens: a snapshot ghost of the row travels from its old frame to its new frame, crossfading the old face into the new one while a green checkmark slides across the row. Holds the shared RowGlideAnimator store, the window-wide RowGlideLayer that draws in-flight glides, the private RowGlideView keyframe animation, and a FrameShape clip.
key_symbols: enum Glide.Direction { case settle, case reopen }

Glide stored fields: id: UUID, threadID: UUID, direction, departure: NSImage, arrival: NSImage, departureFill: Double, arrivalFill: Double, from: CGRect, var to: CGRect, bounds: CGRect, launchedAt = Date.now, var hasArrived = false, var hasLanded = false
private func hidingCell(_ threadID: UUID) -> ObservedValue<Bool>
private func setHiding(_ threadID: UUID, _ hiding: Bool)
func render<Face: View>(_ face: Face, size: CGSize, colorScheme: ColorScheme) -> NSImage?
private nonisolated static let trailingCheckInset: CGFloat = 36
private nonisolated static let leadingCheckInset: CGFloat = 16
private nonisolated static func smoothstep(_ edge0: Double, _ edge1: Double, _ x: Double) -> Double
calls_into: ObservedValue<Bool>, a per-thread observable cell type defined elsewhere
SidebarThreadRow, named in comments as the source of the check insets and the reader of isHiding
state_owned: private(set) var glides: [Glide] - the in-flight ghosts, observed by RowGlideLayer
@ObservationIgnored private var hidingCells: [UUID: ObservedValue<Bool>] - one observable cell per thread ID, created lazily and kept forever so an observing row keeps seeing the same instance
RowGlideView @State private var hasStarted = false - the keyframeAnimator trigger flipped in onAppear
Glide.launchedAt captured as Date.now at construction
Glide.to is re-targetable by land(); hasArrived and hasLanded are mutable flags
side_effects: Reads NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion and refuses to launch any glide when Reduce Motion is on
Rasterizes SwiftUI views into NSImage snapshots through ImageRenderer at NSScreen.main backing scale, defaulting to 2
Two chained Task.sleep timers per glide in .task: sleep(max(settlingDuration - 0.12, 0)) then arrive(glide.id), then sleep(0.12) then finish(glide.id)
Mutates the shared @MainActor singleton RowGlideAnimator.shared from view lifecycle
No file writes, no network calls, no process launches, no keychain access
platform_assumptions: import AppKit: NSImage, NSWorkspace and NSScreen are AppKit only
NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion is the macOS Reduce Motion accessibility flag
ImageRenderer.nsImage is the macOS specific renderer output, where iOS would use uiImage
NSScreen.main?.backingScaleFactor for Retina rasterization with a fallback of 2
Swift Observation (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored) with @MainActor isolation, and nonisolated statics so the keyframe closure can read spring and the insets off the main actor
SwiftUI keyframeAnimator with SpringKeyframe and Spring.settlingDuration
Top-left origin geometry: ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) and frames measured in the window's own coordinate space
ui_elements: RowGlideLayer: GeometryReader around a ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) of one RowGlideView per glide, framed to proxy.size at .topLeading, with .allowsHitTesting(false) and .accessibilityHidden(true)
Ghost shape: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: Chrome.rowCornerRadius, style: .continuous)
Departure image drawn at the from-frame size and arrival image at the to-frame size, both pinned .topLeading and clipped to the interpolated frame
Departure opacity = 1 - smoothstep(0.2, 0.65, p); arrival opacity = smoothstep(0.35, 0.8, p)
Background under the clip: shape.fill(Chrome.overlay(fill)) with .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.28 * lift), radius: 10, y: 4)
Check glyph: Image(systemName: settles ? "checkmark.circle.fill" : "checkmark.circle") with .font(Chrome.inlineIconFont) and .foregroundStyle(Chrome.success)
Check scale: settles ? 1.35 - 0.35 * smoothstep(0, 0.5, p) : 1
Check opacity: settles ? 1 - 0.2 * p : 1 - smoothstep(0.55, 0.9, p)
Check position x = checkStart + (checkEnd - checkStart) * smoothstep(0.05, 0.95, p), y = frame.midY
Check insets measured from the row edge to the check centre: trailing 36 beside the ellipsis while open, leading 16 at the front once settled
Ghost positioned with .position(x: frame.midX, y: frame.midY), then framed to the canvas at .topLeading and clipped with FrameShape(frame: glide.bounds) so it cannot escape the list's visible frame
feature_notes: Two directions: .settle moves the row down to the settled rows with the check travelling trailing to leading as a filled checkmark.circle.fill, and .reopen moves it back up among the open ones with the check travelling leading to trailing as a hollow checkmark.circle that fades out
launch() refuses when from.width <= 1 or from.height <= 1, and refuses entirely when Reduce Motion is enabled
launch() removes any existing glide for the same threadID before appending, so a thread has at most one ghost in the air
A launch is aimed at a fallback rect just past the list's edge, so if the new row never reports a frame the ghost slips out under the clip instead of landing

land() re-targets a glide only when the glide exists, is younger than the 0.5 second landingWindow, and its direction matches the settled flag; the latest report inside the window wins and the interpolation absorbs the re-targeting
Per-thread ObservedValue<Bool> hiding cells mean a launch, landing or finish re-renders only the two rows of that glide plus the layer, not every row in the list
setHiding writes only when the value actually changes, so a row is never re-rendered for a write that said what it already showed
arrive() runs at settlingDuration - 0.12 seconds and un-hides the real row so it shows under the ghost's last frames; finish() removes the ghost 0.12 seconds later, so the handover never shows a gap
finish() re-derives hiding as glides.contains { $0.threadID == threadID && !$0.hasArrived }, so a thread relaunched meanwhile stays hidden
Geometry interpolates x, y, width and height linearly in the spring-driven progress p, so the ghost resizes as well as moves between the two row frames
lift = min(smoothstep(0, 0.12, p), 1 - smoothstep(0.7, 1, p)): the row lifts within the first 12 percent of the flight and has set back down through the last 30 percent
fill = max(departureFill + (arrivalFill - departureFill) * p, 0.12 * lift), so an unfilled row still shows a faint plate at up to 0.12 while airborne
smoothstep is t * t * (3 - 2 * t) with t = (x - edge0) / (edge1 - edge0) clamped to 0...1
The keyframe track is a single SpringKeyframe(1.0, spring: RowGlideAnimator.spring) from an initial value of 0.0, triggered by hasStarted flipping true in onAppear
render() snapshots any Face view at the given size, aligned .topLeading, with the colorScheme forced into the environment so a ghost matches the theme it was captured in
hasLanded is set by land() but is never read anywhere in this file
unresolved_questions: Chrome.glideSpring's exact spring parameters, and therefore settlingDuration and the real flight duration, are defined outside this bundle
Numeric values of Chrome.rowCornerRadius, Chrome.inlineIconFont, Chrome.success and the Chrome.overlay(_:) mapping are outside this bundle
ObservedValue<Bool> is used but defined elsewhere; that it is an observable box is inferred from the comments only
Glide.hasLanded is written by land() but never read here, so whether another file reads it could not be established from the assigned files
The call sites of launch() and land(), presumably SidebarThreadRow or the sidebar list, and where RowGlideLayer is mounted in the window, are outside this bundle
hidingCells is never pruned, and whether that is an intentional bounded cache or a leak over long sessions cannot be judged from this file alone
